message:
This PR centralizes the Android command line tools version reference to establish a single source of truth and eliminate version duplication across the repository.

## Problem
The Android cmdline-tools version "11076708" was hardcoded in multiple locations:
- `scripts/install_minimum_android_sdk_prerequisites.py`
- `.github/workflows/build-app.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/release-app.yaml`

This created maintenance overhead and risk of version inconsistencies when updating the tools.

## Solution
Added `android-cmdline-tools = "11076708"` to `gradle/libs.versions.toml` and updated all consumers to read from this central location:

**Python Script Changes:**
- Added `get_android_cmdline_tools_version()` function to read from libs.versions.toml
- Included robust fallback mechanism for error handling
- Added clear documentation directing maintainers to update only the version catalog

**GitHub Workflows Changes:**
- Added steps to extract version dynamically from libs.versions.toml using grep
- Updated SDK installation steps to use the extracted version
- Applied to both build-app.yaml and release-app.yaml workflows

## Benefits
- **Single source of truth:** All version references now come from gradle/libs.versions.toml
- **Easier maintenance:** Future cmdline-tools updates require changing only one file
- **Consistency:** Eliminates risk of version mismatches across different components
- **Documentation:** Clear comments guide future maintainers

## Testing
- Verified Python script correctly reads version from libs.versions.toml
- Tested workflow version extraction using grep commands
- Confirmed gradle lint task runs successfully with changes
- Validated fallback mechanism in Python script works as expected

Future Android cmdline-tools version updates now only require editing the version in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`.
